tldr: Lean and Mathlib issued a formal certification of a major proof claim, and open-source model tooling advanced through Transformers and llama.cpp releases; these publisher statements must not be confused with independently benchmarked model capabilities.

Five November 19 research preprints explore small-agent planning, scoring, human oversight and video models. Results remain author-reported, three inaccessible journalism reports stay unpublished and all proposed catalog additions remain under review.

news.title: Lean and Mathlib teams certify a formal proof of the Riemann hypothesis
news.summary: A November 21 joint Lean/Mathlib statement reports independent checks of Levent Alpöge's enormous Lean proof released November 20, including statement matching and multiple proof kernels. Alpöge credits collaboration with Claude.
news.why_it_matters: Demonstrates a striking use of AI-assisted mathematics plus machine-verifiable proofs, with independent checks separating a claimed breakthrough from model-generated plausibility.
news.caveat: Formal checking validates a theorem relative to mathematical foundations and the exact statement; independent conceptual exposition and broader mathematical scrutiny can continue. The Lean organizations' certification does not by itself establish how much of the discovery was caused by AI.

news.title: Transformers v5.24 adds native support for looped, audio and multimodal architectures
news.summary: Hugging Face's November 21 v5.24.0 release documents support for Inkling 2 Mini, Apertus 1.5, WavTokenizer, Dory, HY4-VL, Omnilingual ASR and Lara Mini.
news.why_it_matters: New architecture integrations can reduce custom implementation work and give researchers more standard loading paths for varied speech, vision and small-model systems.
news.caveat: This is a library compatibility release, not proof that each model first launched on November 21; weights, gated access, license and device memory vary by model.

news.title: llama.cpp adds Kyutai Hibiki real-time duplex support
news.summary: The ggml-org b12619 release adds mtmd support for Kyutai Hibiki real-time duplex, including a long-session-quality fix and a Metal fusion regression baseline.
news.why_it_matters: Extends local inference plumbing for simultaneous listening and speaking workloads, a distinct path from fixed-turn ASR-LLM-TTS chains.
news.caveat: The release note documents implementation support, not measured end-to-end latency or stability across all devices; specific model checkpoints and compute support must be validated.

news.title: Seer steers small research agents using predicted tool results and action values
news.summary: A November 19 arXiv preprint introduces reusable offline-trained tool-response and value models that score multiple proposed research actions but execute only the selected tool call. Authors report substantial gains on agent benchmarks for 4B/9B Qwen variants.
news.why_it_matters: Suggests a targeted way to spend local compute on action selection rather than hiring a larger reasoning model or paying for every candidate tool call.
news.caveat: Simulator errors can misrank actions; gains are author-reported in studied benchmarks and no production reliability guarantee or universally usable weights were confirmed.

news.title: GLiDE distills reasoning into single-pass calibrated candidate scoring
news.summary: GLiDE proposes 0.4B–27B decision models that score candidate answers without autoregressive reasoning traces, using partial bidirectional attention and soft-target teacher distillation; the paper reports 92.9 ms median single-GPU latency for its 27B configuration.
news.why_it_matters: Potentially useful for low-latency reranking, grading and discrete choices where full answer generation is unnecessary.
news.caveat: Reported scores and timing are from authors' setup, not a head-to-head universal comparison; model-weight/license availability and calibration transfer remain to be checked.

news.title: R2-VLA conditions robot action on calibrated uncertainty and expert intervention
news.summary: The R2-VLA preprint adds a learned uncertainty predictor and task-level failure-risk calibration to retrieval-based robot policy adaptation; authors report 9.2–11.2 percentage-point success improvements on LIBERO suites.
news.why_it_matters: A concrete design for when a robotic agent should request expert help rather than blindly trusting retrieved demonstrations.
news.caveat: Controlled benchmark results and a stated statistical risk threshold do not certify real-world robot safety under distribution shift.

news.title: Expert-drift study adapts human-AI handoffs as expert reliability changes
news.summary: EDA-L2D models recent expert outcomes when deciding whether a model or human should handle a case; authors evaluate simulated shifts in expert reliability on images, medical tasks and hate-speech data.
news.why_it_matters: A useful challenge to the assumption that human oversight is uniformly reliable at all hours and conditions.
news.caveat: A predictive deferral policy is not proof of safe clinical or legal deployment; the study is a preprint with domain-specific evaluation.

news.title: ScaleWorld shares video prediction and high-resolution refinement in one backbone
news.summary: ScaleWorld proposes a causal video architecture that alternates low-resolution future prediction with one-step high-resolution refinement, trained with task-asymmetric on-policy distillation from specialists.
news.why_it_matters: Combining forecasting and refinement may reduce duplicate models and memory costs for interactive video-world applications.
news.caveat: The efficiency/quality tradeoff is author-reported; no broad hardware throughput replication or production license was independently established.
